 In partial results from early voting Tuesday, political newcomer Kristina Knickerbocker was ahead of U.S. Rep. Mike Turner in the race to represent Dayton and the 10th Congressional District, while Cincinnati Rep. Greg Landsman also had an early lead
 Just before 8:30 p.m. Tuesday, Turner, R-Dayton, had 38.49% of the vote while his Democratic opponent stood at 59.79%, according to unofficial results posted by the Ohio secretary of state.
 Eighty-two of 88 Ohio counties were reporting absentee vote totals. Just 2.66% of election day precincts had reported.
 In Ohio’s 10th district, Republican incumbent Turner faced Yellow Springs resident Knickerbocker in her first election. Former Huber Heights City Council member Thomas McMasters was also on the ballot as a Libertarian candidate.
 ELECTION RESULTS: Local vote counts in your area McMasters was at 1.7%, as of 8:22 p.m. Tuesday.
 The district will look new in the next Congress due to redrawn boundaries. Greene and Montgomery counties remain, but the northeastern corner of Butler County has been added, including Middletown and Trenton, cities currently represented in the 8th District.
 Turner, 66, sought his 13th term in the House of Representatives. The former two-term Dayton mayor has never lost a congressional election. A senior member of the House Armed Services Committee and the Oversight Committee, Turner placed protection of Wright Patterson Air Force Base personnel and missions near the top of his political to-do list.
 Knickerbocker, 35, defeated five candidates in the May primary to get to Tuesday’s ballot. She worked as a neuro-oncology nurse practitioner at Ohio State University’s Wexner Center and is a former Air Force officer.
 The 10th District race was closely watched. The Cook Political Report, which weighs competitive House races, changed its rating of the district in the race’s closing weeks from “likely R (Republican)” to “lean R,” meaning the Republican incumbent could be expected to win, but that the race was tightening, from Cook’s perspective.
 Turner won the seat in 2024, beating Democrat Amy Cox by more than 18 percentage points.
 In the state’s First Congressional District, Cincinnati Democrat U.S. Rep. Greg Landsman ran against Republican Eric Conroy.
 In Ohio’s First Congressional District, Cincinnati Democrat U.S. Rep. Greg Landsman, right, ran against Republican Eric Conroy.
 Contributed 
 Conroy is an Air Force veteran and a former CIA agent who had been campaigning with House Speaker Mike Johnson in recent days.
 The district includes Clinton and Warren counties and parts of Hamilton County.
 Early Tuesday evening, Landsman stood at 62.49% while 35.6% of the votes went to Conroy. Libertarian Eric Weise was at 1.91%.
